chunks: Ahmad ibn 'Abdun narrated to me from Ali ibn Muhammad ibn al-Zubayr, from Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Faddal, from Ibrahim ibn Abi Bakr ibn Abi Sammak, from Zakariyya al-Mu'min, from Isma'il ibn 'Ammar, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

He who fasts Ramadan has the choice to break his fast at any time between dawn (fajr) and sunset (maghrib), and for voluntary fasting, he has the choice to break it at any time between dawn and sunset.

key_terms.زَوَالِ الشَّمْسِ: Decline of the sun (noon/dhuhr time, often used as start of day in this context)

ai.seo_question: When can one break their fast during Ramadan or voluntary fasting according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Isfabar delineates the precise temporal boundaries for nullifying a fast, distinguishing between the obligatory Ramadan fast and voluntary (nafl) fasting. It establishes that for both types, the discretion to break the fast extends from dawn until sunset, reflecting the juristic consensus that the prohibition of eating and drinking is lifted once the sun sets, thereby allowing flexibility in fulfilling the daily obligation or supererogatory act.
